checks.title: Every file has exactly one owner, and the owner is a declared role
Project files, the solution, composition, shared configuration, dependency manifests, CI and deployment are owned by integration

Compile order is predefined: each file depends only on earlier files of its project or on referenced projects, project references (source and test) are acyclic, and every test file is in a declared test project

Every interface has a complete contract implemented by one file its producer owns, in file order; its producer tests are in files the producer owns and every consumer has a contract test in a file it owns
Each state machine's states and events are exactly the cases of the state and input unions of one interface (no new state, no unmapped event)

The GitHub error matrix covers every required class and timeouts; a shared HTTP status is never the only evidence and no two such classes share evidence; each class retries within its own bound; every test exists in the plan and belongs to the class's requirements

The Forma layout contract uses only custom properties, classes, patterns and breakpoints of the published Forma release, names no colour literal without a requirement source, and the committed inventory equals the one extracted from the package
Coordination telemetry defines every required metric with a source, keeps textual conflicts apart from semantic failures, and records an unavailable metric as null with a reason, never inferred
The verification execution plan places every (obligation, test) binding of the plan, and every contract, state-machine and unit test, in exactly one suite, keeping each test and its assertions
Every requirement, P0 obligation and test binding of v4 is preserved unchanged
No v4.1 input or document imports or names application source from an earlier rehearsal (Rehearsals 1-6)

Every state machine is deterministic by reviewed guard partitions, every pair is decided (listed or fail-closed), every transition is sourced, every state is reachable, no state is added, and every transition v4.1 adds to v4 names an owner decision and approval

The adjusted DAG is acyclic, keeps every v4 task with its requirements and every v4 ordering not explicitly waived, keeps every estimate at least half of v4's, and labels every change an estimate with a rationale
Every test identity (plan, contract, state-machine, unit) names an owned test file, or is a Praxis record that is not code

Every critical Forma layout rule has executable browser assertions, each exported by the layout kit with a broken fixture that must fail, run against published Forma patterns at contract viewports; every Forma gap has a remedy that uses only Forma tokens

The test tooling is a well-formed owner lock: each lock names a dependency-lock decision and its approval, each entry is an exact id@version, no package is locked twice, and the NuGet packages go to exactly the test projects that host .NET tests (the offline suite compares each lock with the owner's record)
